# The feature ledger, in full

270 features from 104 designs of the main tournament's thirteen rounds, found by scouts who looked at every design's pages and read every judge. GEMS come from designs that finished in the lower half of their round (173): the small good ideas lost with their package. Each lineage's graft takes at least one gem every round. A design's files and screenshots are in tour/gallery/index.json. Find an entry by its number (L001...).

### L001 Deep-set tube in a lifted case (colour or material, GEM)
From **01-softground Soft Ground**, round 1 (4.0, #12 of 12).
- What: The case round each monitor is lifted a step (`.crt` gradient #28322d to #202823 to #1b221d, surface #1d2421) while the glass stays today's pitch black (glass mix on #060a08). Each screen reads as a dark tube sunk into a lighter surround, like a real IBM 5151, rather than a black box on a black page.
- Files: Palette: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/palettes/01-softground.json (surface steps; screen and glass untouched). Sheet: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/out/01-softground/style.css line 1142 `.crt` background gradient, line 1139 `--phosphor-glass`.
- Shot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/out/01-softground/shots/login.png (the sign-in face in its lifted case; lost.png too)
- Praise: Soul 4.5: "the deep monitors set in the lighter surround are a nice touch." Its designer: "the screens look even more like dark tubes set into the page." Otherwise last place.
- Caveats: It got there by lifting the whole ground, which greyed the black into 'stock slate dark mode' in every lens. Lift only the case or the bay that holds a tube, and keep the page at #0b0e0d so the green still jumps off a switched-off screen.
- Suits: Switchboard: the rack's cells in a lighter slate, each holding black glass. Flight Console: grey console bays with the tubes sunk into them. Track: the slate diagram board round the Next up tube. Figure Ground: the figure's screen sunk into its plate.

### L002 Stacked glass panes with glinting edges (colour or material, GEM)
From **06-bottleglass Bottle Glass**, round 1 (4.7, #10 of 12).
- What: Surfaces are drawn as sheets of dark bottle glass. Each layer up is lighter, more chromatic and a little greener (bg #051010 at h196, surface #0a1c1c, surface-2 #0f2322, surface-3 #152b29 at h188). The hairlines carry more chroma and a greener hue than the faces (line #1c3632, line-2 #284641, edge #557873), so card and bubble borders glint like the edge of a pane, and the family's bubbles become lighter teal panes.

Sheet: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/out/06-bottleglass/style.css :root tokens, line 1427 `.said-them .bubble`, `.panel`, `.card`.
- Shot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/out/06-bottleglass/shots/login.png (the sign-in card as a pane; chat.png for the teal bubbles)
- Praise: Style 6: "the boldest and most memorable ground, stacked panes of bottle glass with glinting edges, and it clearly has an idea." Product 5: "tinted glass surfaces and teal chat bubbles look premium at first." Its designer measured hue entropy up 45-100% on every page.
- Caveats: Applied to the whole page it turned everything teal: 'the deep sea' in place of 'the Matrix', one colour family, and the green jumping less (feedback 4.5, skeptic 3). Use it on one family of objects over the green-black page, as a lens or a single readout panel, and keep the page's neutrals as they are.
- Suits: Switchboard: each cell's lamp as an illuminated glass lens, a pane that brightens when lit. Flight Console: the readout strip as a layered glass instrument window. Track: the lamp lenses on the diagram. Pocket: the handheld's screen glass in layers over its four greens.

### L003 The brand is never a kind (colour or material, GEM)
From **08-colourmonitor Colour Monitor**, round 1 (5.5, #7 of 12).
- What: Outings stop sharing the signature green. Outing gets its own colour, turquoise #43dbd0 (the light cyan of an EGA screen), so any green on an idea card or in 'Lately added' means the brand and nothing else. The rest of the kind set takes a colour monitor's phosphors, deeper and more saturated rather than pastel: ideas violet #b188fe, plans sky #6ac4fb, to do yellow #f6d94f, people #fdae4f, shows #fd82ba, seasons #fc8d5e. Every CVD distance improves (kinds 13.6 to 15.8 typical, 5.2 to 9.2 protan). Pine and Alpenglow's glacier-lake teal outing (#65d1da, round 2) is the same move.
- Files: Palette: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/palettes/08-colourmonitor.json (outing, ideas, plans, todo, people, shows, seasons). harness/theme.py rewrites `.kind-outing { --kind: var(--outing); }` and `:has(.kind-outing) { --accent: var(--outing); }`. Round 2 variant: rounds/r2/palettes/r2-rand-1.json (outing #65d1da).
- Shot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/round1/out/08-colourmonitor/shots/home.png (Lately added: the turquoise Outing label)
- Praise: Product 6.0: "The best idea as a system for a family app ... outings get their own turquoise so the brand stops doubling as a kind ... Keep the turquoise outing and the richer sections, which are a real gain for the system." Product notes' synthesis: "08's outing with its own colour, so the brand is never a kind." Style, round 2, on Pine: "keep the glacier-teal outing, which is lovely."
- Caveats: In small labels only, it is invisible at a glance (feedback 5). Turquoise can read as a second blue beside trips' sky, or as more green to some eyes. The tritan pair show~seasonal fell to 5.4. The round 2 lesson says moving learned section colours costs points, so change outing and leave the sections the family knows. Lantern Night's persimmon outing showed that warm hues work for a kind only as small solids.
- Suits: All six have kind marks. Track: a stop's lamp ring in its kind colour, never green. Figure Ground: kind symbols in the figures' legends. Flight Console: the crew board's kind tags. Switchboard: the Ideas cell's breakdown by kind. Timetable: the enamel line colours stay apart from the phosphor. Pocket: the cartridges' labels.

### L004 Two inks: phosphor for the machine's voice, blue-black for the family's hand (colour or material, GEM)
From **r4-rand-3 Kitchen Clock**, round 4 (5.56, #7 of 12 in round 4).
- What: One rule for colour by author. Kitchen Clock limits blue-black ink to what the family writes and touches: fields (#0b121a), date tiles and 'in N days' pills (#1b2633), their chat bubbles, links (#79a0c5) and the current tab. Cards, lines and the case stay the room's colour, and the machine's things stay green. Sonar Watch states it as 'the family's hand is ink, the machine's is phosphor', with a logbook ink (--log #141d27, --log-edge #263444, --log-ink #9eb4ca) on the family's bubbles, names, times and date leaves. Composing Room puts it in the names: 'Vera' in sage mono on her lines, the family's names in blue pencil.

From **r5-rand-4 Night Sleeper**, round 5 (4.24, #12 of 12).
- What: A 2px coloured stripe runs under the top bar, over the phone's tab bar and along the foot's rule, like the livery band along a train carriage. The whole page is framed in one colour line without tinting anything else. It replaces the coloured top glow with a solid line.

### L006 Family chat bubble as sewn cloth (colour or material, GEM)
From **r5-rand-4 Night Sleeper**, round 5 (4.24, #12 of 12).
- What: The family's chat bubble is a cloth patch: a faint 45° twill texture over a solid, with a seam stitched 6px inside its edge. Vera's bubble stays smooth glass, so the two voices are told apart by material (handled cloth against lit glass) as well as by side. This matters because Chat changed least in every entrant.
- Files: Palette /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r5/palettes/r5-rand-4.json (css): token `--twill: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, rgb(255 236 222/.032) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3.5px)`; `.said-them .bubble{background:var(--twill), var(--cloth);border-color:var(--cloth-edge)}`; seam `… .said-them .bubble{outline:1px dashed var(--stitch);outline-offset:-6px}` (--stitch rgb(222 149 138/.22)).

- Praise: Not praised by the judges. They marked the stitching down because dashes read as 'pending', and the madder as maroon. The designer: 'The family's chat bubbles really read as stitched denim patches.'
- Caveats: The dashed seam collides with the app's dashed border for a pending bubble: use a solid or finely dotted inset hairline at low alpha instead. Put it on the family's bubble only, never on every card (that was the confetti). Use slate cloth (#1d2330), never madder. Twill at 1x can alias, so keep alpha at or below .03.
- Suits: Pocket Timeline: the family's words as a soft sewn patch beside the machine's glass screen, tactile and toy-like. Night Timetable: the family's stops on her line set apart by material, not only by colour.

### L008 Solid tiles with no outlines, outlines returned for high contrast (colour or material, GEM)
From **r6-rand-2 Night Herbarium**, round 6 (5.36, #7 of 12).
- What: What the family keeps is a matte solid tile with no border at all. Only a faint top-edge light and a bottom shadow separate it from the ground, so cards, panels and tabs read as objects rather than boxes, and the page loses a layer of line noise. On hover a tile lifts and gains an accent edge. Under `prefers-contrast: more` every tile gets its outline back.

### L009 Grained cabinet case (rebuild as brushed metal) (colour or material, GEM)
From **r7-rand-3 Headland Light**, round 7 (5.01, #11 of 12).
- What: Every monitor sits in a real-looking cabinet: a 97-degree repeating-gradient grain over a three-stop vertical gradient, a chin, a vented grille drawn as a 3rem strip of 2px bars, and a brand-green power light with a small halo. The case becomes a material object with a surface, not a grey rounded rectangle.
- Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r7/palettes/r7-rand-3.json css: `.crt { padding:.75rem .75rem 2.2rem; border-radius:26px 26px 32px 32px; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(97deg, rgb(0 0 0/.07) 0 2px, transparent 2px 7px, rgb(255 255 255/.025) 7px 8px, transparent 8px 13px), linear-gradient(180deg,#57413a,var(--walnut) 45%,#33241f); border-color:#5e4840; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.12), inset 0 -3px 7px rgb(0 0 0/.35), 0 30px 50px -30px rgb(0 0 0/.95), 0 0 70px -40px color-mix(in srgb,var(--phosphor) 40%,transparent) }`, `.crt::before` (grille: `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(0 0 0/.45) 0 2px, transparent 2px 5px)`), `.crt::after` (power light with `0 0 6px color-mix(in srgb,var(--brand) 70%,transparent)`).
- Shot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r7/out/r7-rand-3/shots/login.png (also ideas.png)
- Praise: soul 4.9: 'The walnut cabinets with grain and chin are an authentic 70s touch.' style 5.6: 'The walnut cabinets on the monitors ... are charming and have real personality.' The style notes list 'Headland Light's cabinet grain (on Sign in and 404 only)' among the seed traits worth one more try.
- Caveats: As wood it failed: 'kitsch' (skeptic, system, lessons.md), 'steampunk rather than period CRT' (feedback 3.2), and brown, which the owner rejects. Keep the technique, not the wood. Use a fine horizontal brushing (0-2deg, 1px lines every 3-4px at 2-4% light and dark) over a graphite or pewter gradient (#4a4f55 to #34383d). Use it only on the one monitor that stands alone (Sign in, 404, or Home's Next up), so it reads as the machine's body and not as texture all over the page.
- Suits: console: brushed-aluminium bays and bezels, true to a 1969 flight console, and a material that carries grounded colour without paint. switchboard: the Minitel's moulded plastic case around its terminal, a fine texture in place of the brown keys the lineage lost. pocket: the handheld's plastic shell, drawn thin, instead of the chunky beveled cartridges.

- What: Every printed figure (counts, drive times, due leaves, initials, day numbers) is coloured by its owner (a kind, a section or a role), but at one fixed value: --fig-ink is oklch(from owner 0.68 c*0.92 h). Folios use --folio-ink at L 0.55 and chroma times 0.72. Relative colour keeps each hue exact and its chroma, where a colour-mix toward the green-tinted graphite rotated heather toward blue and rose toward salmon. A row of figures in different hues reads as one set of inks. With prefers-contrast: more both inks switch to full colour.

Palette: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r13/palettes/r13-wmut-1.json
- Shot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/gallery/r13-wmut-1/ideas.png

### L089 Mint core, deep emerald bloom (light effect, GEM)

- What: Every bright core keeps today's #6dff9c, but its bloom is a deep saturated emerald (#12a472, hue 162, L 0.64) instead of a whitish mint fog. Its wrapper carries four stacked drop-shadows: a 0.7px and a 1.2px bone-white edge, like a torn fibre catching the light, then 26px and 70px phosphor spills. So the green leaks out onto the surface round the opening, and the opening has a pale lip. Inside the opening the kit is complete: scanlines, a sheen, a vignette, a 0.35px blur on the text lines, and reverse-video labels kept crisp above the scanlines.

## After tour round 1

Tour round 1 was judged in two heats by the eight lenses: heat a (track, timetable, pocket; 16 designs) and heat b (figure, console, switchboard; 14 designs), each with the yardsticks 00-current (5.00 in a, 4.76 in b) and r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined (7.65 in a, 7.43 in b). Carried to round 2: track, t1-track-graft Track Diagram, Branch Lines (7.84) and t1-track-revival Signal Box Relaid (7.84); timetable, t1-timetable-graft Night Departures (7.56); pocket, t1-pocket-graft Pocket Timeline, Traced (7.71); figure, t1-figure-refine Lit Manual (8.02, the tour's best so far); console, t1-console-graft Lamps and Ladders (7.53, over t1-console-refine at 7.51); switchboard, t1-switchboard-refine Switchboard, Trued (7.84). Every new design's palette is <heat>/palettes/<id>.json, its templates <heat>/variants/<id>/templates/ and its stylesheet <heat>/variants/<id>/sheet.css, where <heat> is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t1-a (heat a) or /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t1-b (heat b). The track entrants keep their stylesheet in variants/<id>/src/ (trued.css, relaid.css, branch.css over track.css, phosphor.css). Strips are <heat>/strips/<id>.png (with -details and -squint), and full-page shots are <heat>/out/<id>/shots/<page>.png. The greeting's titles and what the judges said of them are in tour/titles.md: 'What’s the plan?' is the tour's standard, and 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Lit Manual) is the best-scored alternative.

### Graft results

#### Track series: onto t1-track-graft Track Diagram, Branch Lines (7.84, #1 of 16 in heat a; carried)
- **L033 two-track tape chat**, rebuilt as Chat's double-track main line (her up line, the family's down line, a station and a time for each, the rails merging into one lit line into the box). SPLIT. It took for system ("the best chat in the heat"; the notes: "better than Night Timetable's own"), soul (keep "Chat's rails merging into one lit line into the box"), interaction ("easy to follow") and usability. It read pasted to feedback ("a double-track chat that reads busy"; the notes: "busy in Branch Lines but fine as a meridian in Night Departures"), type (the "centred chat meridian with a right-set 'Vera' title" collides) and style ("Timetable's warm copper version is more inviting than Track's steel double rail"). Fix: one rail with the times in the margin, the title flush left.
- **L143 Status lamp strip with its tally**, rebuilt as the indication shelf (lamps banked by group in a dark well, each a link to its row) with its tally '6 working · 7 off'. SPLIT: the tally took and the lamps did not. Style, type, usability and feedback kept the '6 working · 7 off' figures (T1-23), and soul liked "glowing dots on the black". But "the shelf's lamps have no labels, so they only repeat the list below" (skeptic), "unlabelled lamps, and '7 off' counts keys nobody needs as faults" (interaction), "the Status lamp shelf's lamps have no names" (usability), and "the shelf's floating box on Status ... leaves dead slate" (soul). See Retired.
- **L063 distance dial**, rebuilt as 'The line from home' (T1-22), a lit strip chart of drive times on a square-root scale. TOOK on light and content: feedback ("a glowing 'line from home' built from its own data"), soul ("a real green-screen strip chart"), system, skeptic. Its reading failed: labels collide at 18-21 min (system, type, style, skeptic), and "it is a lookup puzzle" (usability).
- **L145 busy days on the month**, rebuilt as week rails under the month with plan lamps and a lit run from today. DID NOT TAKE: "the week track only reads under the last row" (system), "the week track under the month adds nothing" (interaction), "one line on one row reads arbitrary" (skeptic); feedback notes list "a week track on the month that only shows on the last row" among failed grafts. Soul alone kept "the month's week track with its lit run from today".
- **L186 backlit steel key for 'here'** (a universal fix). DID NOT TAKE: "the backlit steel 'here' key is the loudest non-green thing on the page" (system); the slabs "look disabled and pull the eye to the nav" (skeptic). Retired below; T1-32 replaces it.
- In t1-track-revival (the lineage's first language, revived): **L243 head bracket** TOOK. Feedback 8.9: "The owner's own favourite element is back on every page: the line rings each page icon, drops, turns one 45-degree chamfer and runs under the head's controls"; system: "the line grammar is the most complete in its series". Caveats: the Plans bracket is cramped ("give the month keys their own row", system), and the tabs on the title's rule crowd the head (type). **L209 chat branch ticks and a lit terminus** TOOK as 'your turn' lit where the line meets the box (feedback, soul, style, interaction, usability kept it); soul: give the box Home's resting glow so terminus and box read as one lit stop. **L210 lines only for sequence** TOOK twice: setup as a vertical station line with the next step lit (T1-27) and the fallback as a 45-degree turnout ending at a buffer ("the turnout and buffer stop for 'If that one cannot'", soul; feedback). **L219 terminus rings** took as part of the bracket. **L103 ask box lit from the side** took as the greeting pool (soul: the lit word blooms "over the original greeting pool"). **L239 Sign in and 404 as the two ends of the line**, L137 and L149 were not remarked.
- In t1-track-refine: **L265 drive split and column heads** took only half (type: "direction and duration share one centred Drive column, so 'min' never lines up"; the revival's separate columns are the model, T1-29). **L204 edit form across the row** took as a labelled Edit per To do row (interaction, usability). **L186** on today in the month: usability wants it larger than a 13px chip.

### Retired

- **L186 Backlit steel key for 'here'**: retired. As track-graft's bar key, Open filter and Month key it read as "bright grey-blue slabs that look disabled and pull the eye to the nav" (skeptic), "the brightest non-green shape on the page" (system); the skeptic notes list it among grafts that did not work. The same fault showed in every full steel fill this round: Lit Manual's bar block "is the brightest solid on the page" (feedback) and "a heavy paper slab" (style), and Switchboard, Trued's steel 'today' leaf is "the heaviest thing on the month" (system, skeptic). The system notes' rule: "The 'here' state should be a latched slate cell with a steel cap, never a bright fill." Use T1-32, with L140's LED.
- **L043 LED countdown meter under each plan**: retired as a bar on each row. As console-graft's T-minus ladders they read "as signal strength" (system) and "as signal-strength or battery bars rather than a countdown" (skeptic), and "repeat 'in 4 days' in a code nobody knows" (interaction); usability: "unlabeled codes"; the amber setup ladder "looks like hazard striping" (skeptic). Feedback, soul and style liked them, and soul's three strengths fading with distance or style's 'T-4d' label could still rescue one, but the lineage's own leg lengths (T1-11) say the days in words.
- **L085 Separated-mosaic pictograms that could carry data**: retired as pictures of things. Switchboard, Lamp-lit's bulb, gift, clipboard and figures were "confetti or QR fragments, not data" (skeptic), "decoration at icon size" (system), "look like data but cannot be read" (usability) and "matte, multicoloured and light-less" (soul). Only a mosaic that counts days survives (T1-44).
- **L143 Status lamp strip with its tally**: the unlabelled lamps retire; the tally stays (T1-23). Track-graft's shelf lamps "have no labels, so they only repeat the list below" (skeptic; interaction, usability), and Switchboard, Lamp-lit's 3x3 matrix is "unlabelled dots nobody can read at a glance" (system; interaction, usability, skeptic). Soul liked both as glowing dots. A lamp strip must name its lamps or be a count.
- **L050 Numbered bar ('01 HOME') and the numbered rows of L055's select list**: the numbers retire; the named places and the lit chosen row stay. Every number in the chrome read as a count or as costume this round: '1 Vera 2 Ideas … 5 Wishes' in Night Departures' bar and phone tabs ("reads as counts (there are 12 ideas and 0 wishes)", usability; interaction, feedback, system, skeptic); Timetable Relit's superscript numerals on the nav icons ("the standard unread-badge pattern ('Wishes ⑤' with 0 open)", usability; all eight lenses); Home's section discs running 3, 5, 4, 2 (interaction, skeptic); Live Figures' '01 Home' tabs ("costume", feedback, system, usability); Lamp-lit's '01 Sam' select options ("costume", system; usability); Trued's page numbers 990-999 ("mean nothing to the family", usability). Only type and style kept the inline numerals. A page number may stay on Home's map (switchboard) or on the current key.
- **L037 Readout rail: console clock and zero-padded counts**: the zero-padding retires; the rail stays (T1-12). Every heat b lens marked '05', '02', 'Needs a look 00' and 'Free weekends 00 of 01' as costume on Flight Console, Go and Lamps and Ladders ("tabular figures already align", type).
- **L267 Slashed zero on the tubes**: narrowed. Workbench's slashed zero reads as an 8 ('10 places' looks like '18'; '17:00', '$2.00') (soul, style, system, usability, skeptic, type), and Azeret's is "invisible at 12px" (style, system) and "in prose counts ('0 open') reads like code" (type). Keep a slashed zero only on codes and page numbers, never in prose counts or a heavy raster face.
- **L228 The row afterglow that shows (a steel wash and a lit edge)**: narrowed to the lit edge. Soul: "Row afterglow is a 12% steel wash that no still shows" (track-graft, the same on revival and refine); the soul notes: "Afterglow is the kit effect most often lost this round ... only track-mut shows a clear green fade. Every lineage's standard should state it: a phosphor or sage edge, 1.2s, visible at 120ms." Pocket-graft's kind-coloured amber afterglow failed as well (soul: "amber is 'late' and nothing else"). The steel wash alone does not count; see T1-33.
- **L127 Lit spine with a square node where each section plugs in**: narrowed to pages in time. On Status and Ideas "a spine that plugs in sections is decoration" (skeptic), and a lemon To do spine "blurs amber's one job" (feedback: keep every spine steel).
- **L166 The glass set as a terminal's lines, with double-height headlines**: narrowed to the question. Plan titles at double height break ('Silver / Falls hike') (interaction, skeptic; text-wrap balance did the same on Switchboard, Retyped, type).
- **L018 Cased lens**: narrowed. The pocket entrants' thick rounded graphite lens cases "repeat the owner's 'case too dominant' note" (feedback notes): thin them to a 2-3px bezel with small radii.
- **L255 Late shown on the control itself (an amber tick box)**: questioned, not retired. Usability on Lit Manual: "Keep the late checkbox's frame neutral and put the amber mark beside the words. An amber-framed box reads as a different control state." T1-16's edge bar is the alternative.
- Shown not to work this round, with no ledger entry of their own: pixel display type on page titles (Pocket Relit's Pixelify: "reads as a Game Boy, not a tube", soul; "five voices is too many", type); drawn hardware round the glass (Pocket Instruments' knobs, jacks and speaker: "a false affordance a child will try to press", usability; style would keep one only for the 404 or sign-in); notched, chamfered kind-cap cartridges ("a second, card-game language", style; they "break names mid-phrase", type); wayfinding-yellow links and copper names beside amber late ("three warm hues ... 'late' has to fight for its colour", system; the owner's standing objection to warm browns, feedback notes); Memory, Family and Status hidden under a phone Settings key ("a parent looking for Memory will never open Settings", usability); 'Edit, complete, or snooze' as a button on every row ("a wall of grey text", type); a second way to add beside the primary (interaction, skeptic); halos on body sentences (track-mut: "costs crispness", type notes); synthetic small caps and a fourth face (Cyanotype: rendered "as condensed full caps", system); and sky-cyan links, which make the raw-link fault brighter (Cyanotype, every lens).

## After tour round 2

Tour round 2 was judged in two heats by the eight lenses: heat a (track, timetable, pocket; 16 designs) and heat b (figure, console, switchboard; 14 designs), each with the yardsticks 00-current (4.82 in a, 4.56 in b) and r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined (7.18 in a, 7.26 in b). Every lineage's best new design beat its carried round-1 design, and the lenses marked the carried designs down beside their offspring (t1-figure-refine fell from 8.02 to 6.84, t1-track-graft from 7.84 to 7.04), so a score compares within its heat, not across rounds. Carried to round 3: track, t2-track-graft Lit Sill Line (8.00) and t2-track-refine Branch Lines, Trued (7.91); timetable, t2-timetable-refine Departures, Posted (7.76, over its graft Night Interchange at 7.53); pocket, t2-pocket-graft Pocket Diary (8.03, the tour's best so far); figure, t2-figure-refine Lit Manual, Railed (8.01); console, t2-console-graft Master Caution (7.99, over t2-console-refine Lamps and Legs at 7.87); switchboard, t2-switchboard-graft Switchboard, Patched (7.53). Every new design's palette is <heat>/palettes/<id>.json, its templates <heat>/variants/<id>/templates/ and its stylesheet <heat>/variants/<id>/sheet.css, where <heat> is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t2-a (heat a) or /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t2-b (heat b). The track entrants keep readable sources in variants/<id>/src/ (sill.css for Lit Sill Line, trued.css for Trued, relaid.css for Relaid, Finished, whose built sheet lives only in its palette's css field, and type.css for the Condensed mutant); the switchboard entrants build their sheet from variants/<id>/tools/parts/. Strips are <heat>/strips/<id>.png (with -details and -squint), and full-page shots are <heat>/out/<id>/shots/<page>.png. The greeting's titles and what the judges said of them are in tour/titles.md: heat a's lenses named 'What’s our plan?' best (six of eight), with 'What are we planning?' strongest standing over Lit Sill Line's line of plans but wrapping to two lines in Night Interchange's narrow column; heat b's named 'Tell Vera what to plan.' best (five of eight, the skeptic jointly with 'What are we planning?'; soul, style and system set it level with 'What’s the plan?'); 'Anything to plan?' reads as a yes/no question, 'What shall we plan?' as stiff, and 'What’s next for us?' and 'Tell Vera what’s next.' fail beside a NEXT UP tube.

### Graft results

#### Track series: onto t2-track-graft Lit Sill Line (8.00, #2 of 16 in heat a; 6 top-four, 6 promise; carried)
- **L099 horizon airglow and L098 airglow off the horizon**, rebuilt as the greeting standing on its own Coming up line: the board's foot is the rail, the now lamp breathes at its left end, the run to the Next up tube is lit, the tube's power lamp drops a lit wire to it, and the airglow rises off the lit run (T2-04, T2-05). TOOK, the heat's biggest change. Feedback 8.8: "the greeting standing on the Coming up rail (Pocket's NOW-to-NEXT idea rebuilt as track)" worked. Soul 9: "airglow off the lit run as the one divider (track-graft; lessons asked for exactly this)". Style: "the airglow reworked as light rising off the lit run, since it has a source and a meaning". Skeptic: "the one design where the phosphor and the structure are the same thing". Caveats from nearly every lens: 'Coming up' sits under the sill after its own plates and 'All plans' dangles 40px below the buffer; the tube is read before the question (system, interaction); the plate names wrap to two or three lines.
- **L004 two inks, in L179's midnight form**, rebuilt as 'the family's hand is ink': midnight plates for what the family wrote or put on the calendar, ink wells for every field (T2-06). TOOK on Coming up and the month; questioned in Chat. System: "a grounded companion with a clear rule, better than blue used everywhere". Style: "the best grounded companion in the heat, because it has a job". Feedback: "Lit Sill Line's ink plates are the one clear example" of grounded colour in solid things. But the skeptic lists "navy ink plates in Chat on a double rail" among grafts that did not work ("lean towards an editor's selection blue"), and style: "close to a stock 'selected' navy".
- **L253 lamp-string summary**, rebuilt as Status's lamps typed on the spend tube's glass (T2-07). SPLIT. Soul: "the Status tube carrying the lamp tally in VT323"; feedback: "Status's annunciator moved onto the glass"; system: "Tallies typed on the Status glass". Usability lists it among grafts that did not work: "Lit Sill Line's Status lamps typed on the glass without names (a lookup puzzle)"; interaction: "name each lamp in the tube (Chat, Digest, Keys…)". The L143 rule holds: a lamp string must name its lamps.
- **L110 power-on roll bar**, rebuilt as the route set on opening: a roll down every tube and a white-hot head running the sill from now to the first stop (T2-18). TOOK with soul ("the timetable raster fill and the track-graft sweep are the best power-ons"); not remarked by the others.

T1-33's sage afterglow edge "is still invisible in every still" (soul). T1-22's line from home now names three stations, but pointing at a row to light its station "works only with a mouse" (usability), and the Drive column glued the compass back on ('27 min S', type), a regression from T1-29.
- In t2-track-refine Branch Lines, Trued (7.91, #3; carried): **T1-01 NOW across the list** TOOK on To do ("excellent", interaction; feedback, soul keep it). **T1-27 with usability's rule** (hollow amber rings, the next rimmed in phosphor and named 'Next step') TOOK (interaction, usability). **T1-23 the tally, with a name under every lamp**, TOOK as the Status instrument (T2-10: "the best instrument in the heat", skeptic). **T1-29 the table standard** TOOK with bold figures and light units (T2-11, type). **T1-35 the newest stop lit** and 'your turn' TOOK (soul). **T1-22 finished** SPLIT ("stations named in blooming VT323", soul; "labels collide with the ticks", usability). **T1-21 head figures** HALF: "the labels still stack in two small lines beside the numeral" (type). **T1-33** did not show ("the steel wash doesn't read", soul). Folding the month's past weeks down to one real week read as an empty page (skeptic, usability, system).

### Retired

- **L022 Hatched coloured-pencil swatches as the kinds' legend**: retired. As Gauged Manual's kind squares and Kind bars they read as "grey noise" that "remove the only colour in the content" (style), "indistinct and look disabled" (system), "near-identical brown hatches" at 1x (skeptic), "merge the kinds" (interaction), "harder to tell apart than solid ones" (usability) and "fussy and muddy" (feedback). Only soul kept them ("grounded and matte"). Use flat, matte, low-chroma squares (T1-30).
- **L167 Dimension lines for 'from now'**: retired. Measured from a NOW datum on every Coming up row, they were "ruler noise" (soul), "clutter" (style), "drafting noise over leaders that already do the job" (system), they "break the clean right edge of the relative column" (type), "look like a scale and are not one" (interaction), are "decoration the row already says" (usability), "ornament" (skeptic) and "fussy" (feedback). The survey scale under a tube (T2-27) is the one dimension that earned praise, and only as a drawing of the whole four weeks.
- **L014 Rules that take their part's colour**: retired as the carrier of a section's colour. Switchboard, Patched's circuit colours in frames, leaders and figures were "too thin by area to offset the green tubes" (feedback), "too faint to count on a dim display" (soul), and "frames plus leaders make a wireframe" (skeptic). Style alone kept "the circuit-coloured hairlines". Colour needs a solid with a job (T2-06, T2-36).
- **L108 Stepped three-frame afterglow on rows**: retired as a way to make the row afterglow show. Pocket Diary's steps(4) over 1.2s "doesn't show" (soul) and "barely shows" (system). The phosphor edge held on a long-persistence curve (T2-15) is the version the stills catch.
- **L146 Four shapes with their key in the footer** (with L135): narrowed to the pages whose marks need a key (Status, Settings). In every footer it "reads as fine print" and is "legal print nobody will read" (style), "a smell" ("shapes that need a legend on every page", skeptic) and "a system crutch, though a coherent one" (system), and feedback counts it among grafts that did not work; usability: "a design that needs a key on every page has too many marks". Soul, interaction and usability kept it for teaching. The better answers are a word beside every lamp (heat b's usability notes) and a tally that is its own legend (T2-24, T2-34).
- **L050 Page numbers**: narrowed further. Round 1 left a page number on Home's map; the switchboard entrants' 200-990 codes are still "a code the family must learn to ignore" (interaction), "costume" (system, skeptic) and "nobody navigates by them" (usability), on Home's map and in the heads alike. Leave them off, or at half strength in the bar at most.
- **L186 Backlit steel key for 'here'**, again: Lamps and Legs' pale steel 'here' slab is "the loudest non-green thing in the bar and 'more blue than necessary'" (feedback) and "heavy" (style). Its sibling's dark latched key with the jewel (T1-32 with L097) is the fix.
- **L201 Point at a row, its mark lights**: questioned for touch, not retired. Every version this round (Lit Sill Line's line from home, Trimmed's pulses, Patched's radar numerals) lights only on hover and keyboard focus; "works only with a mouse" (usability). Light the mark on focus-within and on a tap too.
- **T1-20 and T1-09, amber on the green glass**: questioned. Soul (heat b), on Patched's To do tube: "don't set amber 'Late' on the green glass; a monochrome tube shows urgency by inverse video, which keeps amber for the paper side of the page". System, on Lamps and Legs: make Today the only lit window and Late an amber numeral in the rail's type. Feedback and soul still liked that design's amber Late window, so it stands as one lit alarm at most.
- Shown not to work this round, with no ledger entry of their own: a chat whose dotted leaders run the width of the thread to the speaker (Lit Manual, Railed's ~950px leaders "rule the thread like notepaper", style; faulted by all eight lenses); dotted leaders through every row of every register ("Leader fatigue", skeptic; type: "A leader should bridge a gap the eye cannot jump, not draw a rule through the reading"); an amber head count for routine calls (Pocket Diary's '6 worth a look', seven lenses: amber is for what someone can act on); a lamp lit green for a part that needs a look (Status's 'This page' on the figure and switchboard entrants: "The light lies", skeptic; system, interaction, usability); a head tube spanning every inner page (Switchboard, Settled at 72% green: feedback, soul, style, system, skeptic); a green pool spreading over the greeting plate (both consoles and Settled: "the 'wash in the corner' the owner rejected", skeptic; system); folding the month down to one real week (Trued: skeptic, usability, system); boxed state chips on every row (Night Interchange's service board: interaction, type, system, skeptic, style); a second rail beside the page's rail (Night Interchange's General: feedback, style, usability); ways to start drawn like fields (Trued: system, skeptic); the question squeezed beside the radar on the glass (Patched: interaction, usability); a power-on over the glass that holds the question and the field (Patched: interaction); true small caps from a fourth face, with a wider mono (Ladders, Reset: Barlow Condensed's small caps "read as tracked caps" at 8.7px glyphs, and Azeret's slashed zeros made the zero-padding louder, every lens); a universal dotted zero with tabular figures in prose (Branch Lines, Condensed: "fussy" in Vera's words, style; type, usability), and a Plex Condensed swap that "moves it towards IBM's Carbon look" (style); 72px drawn emblems and dimension ticks on every head rule (Surveyed: "costume", every lens); square-cut, section-coloured place legends in the bar ("a rainbow ... a costume", skeptic; system, style, soul); denim secondary keys ("too faint to guide anyone", usability; "look disabled", skeptic); half-weight easing of lit text ("nearly invisible at size", type; "slightly less alive rather than calmer", soul); a 5:1 panorama tube (soul; see T2-26); and violet for the route (Master Caution: "off-period", feedback; "a hue without a job", system; style dissented).

## After tour round 3

Tour round 3, the tour's last developing round, was judged in two heats by the eight lenses: heat a (track, timetable, pocket; 16 designs) and heat b (figure, console, switchboard; 14 designs), each with the yardsticks 00-current (4.56 in a, 4.29 in b) and r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined (6.79 in a, #10 of 16; 6.65 in b, #9 of 14). Every lineage's best new design again beat its carried round-2 design, and the lenses again marked the carried designs down beside their offspring (Pocket Diary fell from 8.03 to 6.74, Lit Sill Line from 8.00 to 6.94, Lit Manual, Railed from 8.01 to 6.68, Master Caution from 7.99 to 6.57, Departures, Posted from 7.76 to 6.42, Switchboard, Patched from 7.53 to 6.33), so a score compares within its heat, not across rounds. Each lineage's final, carried to the closing comparison with where it started: track, t3-track-refine2 Trued, Relit (7.75, #1 of 16) and t3-track-graft Sill Line, Ticked (7.52, #2); timetable, t3-timetable-refine Departures, Platformed (7.36, #3, over its graft Departures, Printed at 7.21); pocket, t3-pocket-refine Pocket Diary, Kept (7.31, #4, over Pocket Diary, Lit at 7.04 and Diary in Ink at 6.76); figure, t3-figure-refine Lit Manual, Relit Rails (7.56, #1 of 14, over Wired Household at 7.32); console, t3-console-graft Waypoint Lamps (7.40, #2, with every lens's promise vote, over Caution, Cleared at 7.11); switchboard, t3-switchboard-refine Switchboard, Settled Light (7.22, #4, over Patched Through at 6.74). This round a refinement led five lineages of six: the judges rewarded finish over new devices. Of the six grafts only Waypoint Lamps led its lineage (Sill Line, Ticked was carried as the track series' second); Printed, Diary in Ink and Patched Through each lost on one or two pasted parts, and Wired Household split the lenses over Fig. 0. Every new design's palette is <heat>/palettes/<id>.json, its templates <heat>/variants/<id>/templates/ and its stylesheet <heat>/variants/<id>/sheet.css, where <heat> is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t3-a (heat a) or /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t3-b (heat b). The four track entrants ship a minified sheet.css; read their sources in variants/<id>/src/ (relit.css for Trued, Relit; ticked.css for Sill Line, Ticked; refine.css for Sill Line, Trued; instruments.css, dial_geometry.py and halftone.py for Sill Line, Instrumented, whose signals are static/sig-*.svg). The switchboard entrants build their sheet from variants/<id>/tools/parts/ (g_settled.css and h_light.css for Settled Light; g_patch.css and h_rev3.css for Patched Through; g_mutant.css for Squared). Strips are <heat>/strips/<id>.png (with -details and -squint), and full-page shots are <heat>/out/<id>/shots/<page>.png.

The greeting's titles. Heat a's eight lenses all named 'What’s our plan?' best (style jointly with 'What needs planning?'): short, in the family's own 'our', one phone line, a short lit word that is the job. 'What’s the plan?' was a close second with six ('a little less the family's own'); 'Tell Vera our plans.' was second for soul and the skeptic but read as 'an instruction, not an invitation', and its separately spanned full stop hurt the setting (type, usability); 'What needs planning?' 'cannot be answered no' but lights a heavy 8-letter word; 'What should we plan?' sounds hesitant; 'Anything to plan?' invites 'no' and 'What are we planning?' reads as a status check (all eight). Heat b's eight all named 'Tell Vera what to plan.' best (feedback and soul jointly with 'Tell Vera our plans.'): it names who hears you and the whole job in one verb, the lit word lands at the full stop, and it sets at 52px semibold and 64px light alike. Heat b read 'What’s our plan?' and 'What’s the plan?' as 'show me the plan', the opposite of the box's job (interaction, usability, system, skeptic, soul), and 'Tell Vera our plan(s).' as presuming a plan exists. The two heats disagree on 'What’s our plan?'; neither saw both leaders side by side.

### Graft results

#### Track series: onto t3-track-graft Sill Line, Ticked (7.52, #2 of 16 in heat a; 5 top-four, 1 promise; carried as the series' second final)
- **L042 Setup cut to one line**, rebuilt as a 56px strip: an amber triangle, a short track of three numbered 44px rings (ring 1 lit), a buffer 'All 3 steps' and one link, 'Next: choose your own password' (T3-06). TOOK, the round's most copied graft. Interaction: "the best one-glance setup in the heat ... worth copying across lineages". System: "better than any boxed setup notice in the heat". Style: "setup shrunk to a tiny three-ring track in an amber-edged strip". Feedback: "the one-line setup strip frees Home". Caveats: it hides what each step is for (usability: show the 'so the family can…' clause on hover or at desktop width); amber rings 2 and 3 read as warnings (skeptic: only ring 1 coloured, the rest steel); 'All 3 steps' is set smaller than its row (type).
- **L048 Checkbox drawn as a lamp, with L255 late on the control**, rebuilt as 'the tick is the stop': a transparent 44px button on the To do rail whose ring is steel open, amber late, dashed pewter with no date, sage filled when done (T3-07). SPLIT. Feedback: "the To do ring is the tick you press"; skeptic lists "To do's tick-as-stop" among grafts that worked; style: "To do's dated margin with rings you press makes the line do work". Interaction: "elegant, but the affordance is weak ... an amber ring reads 'late' rather than 'press'"; usability: "a first-timer reads an amber ring as a status lamp, not a button ... the same shape means 'status' elsewhere". See Retired (L048, L255).
- **L122 Quiet weeks folded, with L132 shaded weekends**, rebuilt as a dashed run between two hollow lamps and the weekend a slate step lighter (T3-09). TOOK quietly: feedback, "the dashed quiet week on Plans is a nice touch"; no lens faulted it.
- **L209 Chat branch ticks and a lit terminus**, rebuilt as one 2px steel track, times in a right-aligned tabular margin, the day a slate plate in a break of the track, the family's plates on pewter ticks and the your-turn ring at the box (T3-08). TOOK: feedback, "Chat hangs from a left track with times in the margin and a lit 'your turn' ring". Soul asks the ring to take E4's halo.
- The lineage's fixes: **the question as the board's headline** (T3-04) SPLIT: style 8.5, "the boldest composition"; soul 8.5, "this heat's best balance of light ... one luminous zone, then calm"; but the headline floats top right beside the tube, so the question is not read first (system, interaction, usability, skeptic), and the big lit 'planning' with the tube's airglow "makes the top heavy with light" at about 69% green (feedback; type, system and every titles note on the 8-letter lit word). **The rail's name in a break of the lit run** (T3-05) TOOK (style, soul). **Kind words hung left of their rings in Lately added** SPLIT: "a good typesetter's move" (type), "earn their place" (system); "read as a column of grey" (style), "sit oddly left of the icons" (skeptic). To do's two-line amber margin is too dense (type). Phone starters scroll sideways (usability, interaction).
- In t3-track-refine2 Trued, Relit (7.75, #1 of 16; 7 top-four, 5 promise; the series' first final): **L100's junction that lights while you write**, rebuilt as the 'Or start with' ring of a steel branch off the box (T3-01), TOOK as part of the branch: feedback, "high-style line art"; skeptic, "the best use of the line language"; interaction 8, "the clearest reading order in the heat". **L034 the sunk readout well**, as the time well at each plate's foot (T3-02), TOOK (style: "the most material board in the heat"; interaction, usability). **L132 weekend shading** on the month was not remarked. **T2-08 the line on the month, run under every week**, DID NOT TAKE: "five full rails through the grid read heavy" (feedback), "a rail under every week turns the grid into a subway map" (system), "clutter when you only want a date" (usability); keep the rail on today's week only. Shrinking the tube to a plate's height cost soul ("the monitor is no longer a hero", soul 7; "crammed into the plate row", skeptic) while style and interaction praised the equal plates. The navy plates split again: feedback and style call them grounded colour in the content, the skeptic "big solid slabs that drift toward 'navy UI kit'". Ideas lost its scope ("the one page without line art or phosphor", feedback). The steel setup line is "bland" beside Ticked's strip (style), and Home runs long (interaction: fold setup to Ticked's strip).
- In t3-track-refine Sill Line, Trued (7.04, #7; 2 top-four; not carried): the rail now runs from the now lamp under the tube to the plates "all in reading order" (feedback 8.6), and Status's named lamp board "reads as an instrument" (feedback). But about 100px of dead glass sits beside the tube (every lens but soul), the plates shrank to labels (style), the 24rem lit run is glare that "stabs out of the board's left edge" (system, soul, skeptic), and the amber-outlined setup card reads as an alarm (skeptic).
- In t3-track-mut Sill Line, Instrumented (6.88, #9; 1 top-four, 4 promise), a graphics mutant: the instrument faceplate (T3-10) is the heat's single best object (style, system, soul, skeptic, feedback), the six-signal family (T3-11) split, and the halftone airglow did not show. Everything outside Status is "pixel-identical to the parent" (system, skeptic, feedback), so as a design it fails the owner's 'nearly identical' test; every lens asked for the faceplate in the series' final.

### Retired

- **L164 Relative time as a pencilled margin note**: retired in a script face. Diary in Ink's Victor Mono italic 'pencil' failed with all eight lenses: "a costume rather than handwriting" (feedback), "a costume" (skeptic), "a font demo" (style), "costs readability and adds a fifth face" (system), "slow to read" (interaction), "the hardest text on Home to read for tired eyes" (usability), "drift off the tube's world" (soul). Type alone saw "a real typographic idea with a job ... right idea, wrong face". If 'how far off' is ever set as a hand again, use the body face's or Plex Mono's italic, on Coming up's distances only, never amber stacks.
- **L048 Checkbox drawn as a lamp**: narrowed: the thing you press to mark done must look like a box. Waypoint Lamps' round pilot lamps "read like a radio" and its amber minus "like 'remove' or 'disabled'" (interaction), "break one control, one look" (usability), "a warning" (skeptic); Ticked's ring-as-tick has a "weak affordance" (interaction) and reads as a status lamp (usability). A lamp may glow inside a square well when ticked, or sit beside the row as state. Feedback and soul liked both as "phosphor where the hands go".
- **L255 Late shown on the control itself**: questioned. An amber ring or outline on the tick reads "'late' rather than 'press'" (interaction), "lean[s] toward warning" (system, on Kept) and "shouts" (skeptic, on Settled Light). Keep the box neutral; carry late on the row's amber edge and its words.
- **L021 Separated-block rule**: retired. Patched Through's dashed block caps on every panel were "noise" (system, feedback), "add noise everywhere" (skeptic): one solid 2px cap is enough.
- **L045 Hatched blanking plates**: retired. The household rack's hatched slot read as "a broken control" (interaction), "an unexplained hatched empty box" (usability), "a dead hatched cell" (skeptic), and left the rack "ragged" (feedback). Close an open slot by letting the last cell span, or leave it empty.
- **T2-41 The question at two strengths**: narrowed. Patched Through's 'What’s the' dim in VT323 below body contrast is "a dim smear" (skeptic), "hardest to read" (usability), "only 'plan?' readable at a glance" (interaction), "low contrast" (type). Set the rest of the question at full ink (Plex, or bright VT323) and light only the key word.
- **T2-08 The line on the month**: narrowed to today's week. Trued, Relit's rail under every week "turns the grid into a subway map" (system), "run[s] heavy" (feedback) and is "clutter when you only want a date" (usability).
- **L034 Sunk readout window**: narrowed: as a steel or plain inset well (T3-02) it took; outlined in amber for late it read as buttons and warnings (system, interaction, usability, skeptic, type, soul).
- **T2-06 The family's hand is ink**: questioned again. Feedback and style still call Trued, Relit's ink plates grounded colour in the content, but the skeptic sees "big solid slabs that drift toward 'navy UI kit'" and Diary in Ink's who-tags "navy chips". Ink on plates the tube's height wants toning toward slate with only the cyan cap; ink on small tags wants no fill at all.
- Shown not to work this round, with no ledger entry of their own: a landscape picture behind the box the family types in, with decoy route legs that look like data (Master Caution, Drawn: "clip art", skeptic; "decoration that misstates data", system; every lens); squaring the glass and lamps (Switchboard, Squared: invisible at page scale and greener, every lens); a phosphor halftone airglow ("make the halftone band visible or drop it", soul); a lit prompt or caret in the empty box, which reads as typed text (Pocket Diary, Lit: interaction, usability, system, type, soul); quotation marks round the ways to start (Departures, Hung: "suggest the quotes are sent", system, interaction, skeptic); a three-column Home that squeezes the box (Departures, Hung: feedback, style, system, interaction, skeptic); inverted-green chips for Today, Working or '3 late' ("glare and an editor-theme tic that should go everywhere", skeptic on Caution, Cleared, Waypoint Lamps and Wired Household); taking the next plan out of Coming up's list because the tube shows it (Caution, Cleared: every lens); a tube that says nothing ('nothing dated ahead', 'Nothing dated after the late ones': system, interaction, soul); the next plan said twice, by a tube and the rail's first row (Relit Rails: feedback, interaction, usability, skeptic); a rail lit green along its whole length (Printed and Sill Line, Trued: "glare", system, skeptic); amber outlines and slabs on routine setup (Sill Line, Trued and Ticked, Caution, Cleared, Wired Household: skeptic); starters that scroll sideways on a phone or are hidden there (four heat-a designs, and Settled Light: usability, interaction, soul); invented clock times on due dates with no time ('19:56', type, every heat-a lineage); four or five text faces (Diary in Ink: feedback, system, interaction, type, usability); light 300 section heads (Magazine: they "lose mass on the squint", five lenses); a Row 0 or head tube tinted green across every inner page (Patched Through; round 2's lesson again); and a plum enamel face ("off-period", feedback; "muddy-purple", skeptic).

## After crossing round 14a

Crossing round 14a gave each of the thirteen lines one cross: the line's own idea kept, its judges' most-cited fixes applied, and features of the other camp rebuilt in its own terms. Two heats, eight lenses each, with the anchors 00-current, r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined and t3-track-refine2 Trued, Relit in both; heat b's means are put on heat a's scale (+0.18, from the shared anchors), and the figures below are those linked means. Every cross beat its carried design, by 0.27 (Lit Manual) to 1.02 (Dessau). Heat a (desk, quote, dessau; trued, manual, departures, settled): x14a-trued-cross Trued, Headlamp 7.99 (#1, 8 top-four, 4 promise), x14a-desk-cross Desk Terminal, Patched 7.95 (#2, 7 top-four, 3 promise), x14a-departures-cross Departures, Signalled 7.66 (#3, 5 top-four, 5 promise), x14a-manual-cross Lit Manual, Slotted 7.64 (#4, 4 top-four), x14a-quote-cross Quote Board, Posted 7.58 (#6, 4 top-four), x14a-settled-cross Switchboard, Quoted 7.42 (#8), x14a-dessau-cross Dessau, Wired Through 7.34 (#10, 3 top-four, 7 promise, the most); anchors Trued, Relit 7.60 (#5), Joined 7.45 (#7), today 4.94. Heat b (plate, listing, folio; sill, pocket, waypoint): x14a-waypoint-cross Waypoint, Ruled 7.88 (#1, all 8 top-four), x14a-sill-cross Sill Line, Squared 7.87 (#2, 7 top-four), x14a-folio-cross Folio, Railed Contents 7.78 (#3, 6 top-four, 6 promise), x14a-plate-cross Plate, Engraved 7.68 (#4, 5 top-four), x14a-listing-cross Listing, Lit Through 7.65 (#5, 7 promise), x14a-pocket-cross Pocket Diary, Lit Line 7.57 (#6, 3 top-four, no promise); anchors Trued, Relit 7.47 (#7), Joined 7.41 (#8), today 5.10. Every line carries its cross. Files: heat a in cross/x14a-a, heat b in cross/x14a-b (palettes/<id>.json, variants/<id>/sheet.css and templates/, strips/<id>.png); each cross's plan and borrows are in cross/x14a/stage/plan-<line>.json.

What the lenses said of the crossing itself, in both heats: the best crosses joined a main-camp FRAME or HEAD (the cased terminal, the head row with its figure, rule heads, the needle meter, the status foot) to a tour GRAMMAR (rails with one lit NOW, a lit run from now to next, wires, numerals tied to rows). Main lines gained most by taking the tour's lit lines (Desk's patch lead, Listing's stem, Folio's rails); tour lines gained most by taking the main camp's instruments and heads (Trued's meter, Sill's faceplate, Waypoint's rule heads and head rows). Three warnings ran through both heats: CONVERGENCE (the same title on five heat-a crosses and two heat-b crosses, the same three-ring setup band, the same rail with a NOW lamp and radar Next up tube: style, skeptic, every titles note); COLOUR LOST WITH THE COSTUME (Dessau 88% green, Departures 71%, Desk "close to colourless": "replace the colour, do not delete it", feedback); and the ROW AFTERGLOW still invisible in stills on every design for a sixth round, except Trued's starter rings and Settled's 2px edge (interaction).

Titles. 'Give Vera something to plan.' was the most favoured wording in both heats (heat a: feedback, system, interaction, type, usability best; heat b: feedback, system, interaction, type, usability best or joint best), but it was now on seven crosses and every lens flagged the duplication. Its best settings: one line in condensed bone with 'plan.' hot-cored and the full stop lit (manual-cross; system, type); on the glass with a single block cursor (desk-cross; soul); two lines breaking before 'to' (quote-cross; system, type). 'Tell Vera what to plan.' stayed the skeptic's best and a near-equal for feedback, soul, interaction and usability. 'What needs a plan?' (sill-cross) was heat b's best for the skeptic, soul and usability and close for the rest: it cannot be answered 'no' and its short lit word sits over the lit run. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (trued-cross) is clear but clunky ('needs a'). 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' (dessau-cross) was style's best ("the only title in the heat with personality") and a slogan to the rest. 'What's on for us?' (folio-cross) was style's and soul's best in heat b and failed for interaction, usability, type and the skeptic (it asks to be shown). 'What can we pencil in?' (pocket-cross) is warm but tentative. 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (listing-cross) failed with most ('line up' reads as queueing; a two-word glow block).

### Retired

- **T3-07 / L048 the tick as the stop, again**: retired for good. Desk Terminal, Patched's open amber rings on the To do rail were read as late lamps or radios by usability, interaction and the skeptic, after Ticked and Waypoint Lamps in round 3. Sill Line, Squared's square well sitting ON the rail as the stop took instead (interaction: "the clearest list in the heat"): the box is square, the rail carries it.
- **T3-29 / L193 the placard that names a window's scale**: narrowed to plain words. Plate, Engraved held each to one line naming a true scale and still lost: "instrument jargon a family will not read" (interaction), "oscilloscope units" (usability), "fussy" (soul), "too faint to function" (skeptic), "a fourth label style" (type). Say 'Next 4 weeks' or 'Spend, last 30 days', or drop it where the axis already says '1 wk'.
- **The stencil leak under the lit word** (Plate, Engraved's light-leak cut, the round-13 L106 pool drawn as a short bar): retired with every lens: "reads as an underline or typo" (skeptic), "a stray dash" (feedback, soul, interaction, usability), "a typographic underline" (type). A pool from below has no hard edge.
- **L146 the shape key as a full-width footer strip** (Sill's legend track, Waypoint's shape key): narrowed to one short line per site or per page with lamps (system, style, skeptic, soul).
- **Waypoint rings on a radar whose bearings mean nothing** (Dessau's re-seated half-dial): "a figure that looks like data but isn't misleads, which is worse for comprehension than no figure" (interaction; usability). Put the rings on time (Folio's radius by day, X14a-28, or a straight line of days, X14a-07).
- **The lit word orphaned on its own line in another face** (Settled's VT323 'plan.'): five lenses read a broken wrap. One face, one run.
- **Page numbers in the nav and teletext cross-references** ('Home 100', 'see p400 Plans', Folio): codes to decode (interaction, usability, type, system, skeptic). P-numbers live in the page head only; a starter says 'lands in Plans'.
- **Ring stops beside form fields** (Departures, Signalled's new-idea form): "read as radio buttons a first-timer will try to click" (usability). Only the final lit stop at the submit.
- **Plates stretched to the rail** (Trued, Headlamp's fix): empty graphite with every lens. Size plates to content.
- Shown not to work this round, with no ledger entry of their own: deleting off-period inks without replacing them (Dessau 88% green, Departures 71%, Desk "close to colourless": feedback, soul, style, system, skeptic; replace with steel-cyan, sage, wheat, clay in grounded amounts); every cross taking the same title, setup band and Next up tube (style, skeptic: keep each line's signature); underlined row titles at rest (Quote, Dessau, Waypoint, again); amber as a section colour or control outline (Quote's amber checkboxes and wheat-amber '4', Dessau's scattered triangles, Pocket's amber ring column); amber edge plus triangle plus words for one state (Waypoint: keep the triangle and words); steel-blue plate caps and starter notches leaning navy (Sill, Plate, Desk's latched key); Lit Manual's round dial as a lone badge in a head column (Listing: "a third dial style"); a slot glass taller than its data (Manual: "an empty equaliser"); Home's next plan taken out of Coming up's list into the tube (Quote: plans "start on the 9th"); the board's hover glow in the wire's green (Departures); a second Next tube on Pocket's line; Pocket's boxed right column beside a line whose idea is no boxes; multicoloured kind squares as bullets (Waypoint: "confetti", and a square that is not pressable breaks its own shape law); a lit placeholder frame inside the tube (Folio; principle 3 again).

## After crossing round 14b

Crossing round 14b gave each of the thirteen lines its second cross: the line's own idea kept, its 14a judges' most-cited fixes applied, and features of the other camp rebuilt in its own terms. As in 14a there were two heats of eight lenses each, with 00-current, r13-idea-1 Desk Terminal, Joined and t3-track-refine2 Trued, Relit as anchors in both. Heat b's means are put on heat a's scale (+0.06, from the shared anchors), and the figures below are those linked means. Every cross beat its carried design, so every line carries its 14b cross. The margins run from +0.10 (Departures) to +0.74 (Dessau). The carried 14a crosses scored lower this round than they did in 14a, because they now stood beside their own successors.

Heat a, ranked out of 17:
- x14b-trued-cross Trued, Yard Lit 8.15 (#1, 7 top-four, 4 promise; +0.32 on Headlamp)
- x14b-manual-cross Lit Manual, Dialled 8.05 (#2; in all 8 top fours and all 8 promise lists, the only design to do both; +0.56)
- x14b-desk-cross Desk Terminal, Wired 7.92 (#3, 8 top-four, 0 promise; +0.25)
- x14b-dessau-cross Dessau, Dialled 7.85 (#4, 5 top-four, 7 promise; +0.74, the round's largest gain)
- x14b-quote-cross Quote Board, Lit 7.69 (#6; +0.28; first for type at 8.3)
- x14b-settled-cross Switchboard, Patched 7.65 (#8; +0.43; second for usability at 8.0, last for the skeptic at 7.1)
- x14b-departures-cross Departures, Terminus 7.59 (#9; +0.10; interaction, usability and the skeptic held it level with its parent)
- Anchors: Trued, Relit 7.50, Joined 7.28, today 4.82.

Heat b, ranked out of 15 (linked):
- x14b-waypoint-cross Waypoint, Patched 8.15 (#1, 8 top-four, 4 promise; +0.37)
- x14b-sill-cross Sill Line, Wired 8.12 (#2, 8 top-four, 5 promise; +0.34; feedback 8.4)
- x14b-folio-cross Folio, Fastext 8.06 (#3, 8 top-four, 6 promise; +0.38; first for style and type)
- x14b-listing-cross Listing, Dropped Through 7.85 (#4, 5 top-four; +0.37; second for interaction and type)
- x14b-pocket-cross Pocket Diary, Bound 7.80 (#5, 4 promise; +0.32)

Files: heat a is in cross/x14b-a and heat b in cross/x14b-b, each with palettes/<id>.json, variants/<id>/sheet.css and templates/, and strips/<id>.png plus -details and -squint. Each cross's plan and borrows are in cross/x14b/stage/plan-<line>.json, and its revision notes are in cross/x14b/stage/designs.json.

**The crossing itself.** Every lens in both heats said the camps have met. The top designs pair a tour GRAMMAR (a route, a sill, a line, a rail with one lit NOW, numerals tied to rows) with a main-camp FRAME (rule heads, head rows, a readout, a status foot, a case). The tour lines gained most by taking frames: Trued's rule heads and foot, Sill's foot, Waypoint's lead. The main lines gained most where a circle or a glass was finally made to report real data: Dessau's dial, Folio's Row 0 and slide rule.

**Light.** The lit lead now took on six lines, all in the corrected short, straight form. Soul b: "every cross beat its carried parent, and all by the same mechanism: light now goes somewhere". Three new written light rules were credited as the round's main system gain (system a):
- Manual: one lit stroke a page.
- Desk: one light per band.
- Quote: a figure that counts is ink, a figure that is live is light.
Style b would make a fourth the standard: Folio's "phosphor only on glass".

**Faults.** Two faults ran through both heats:
- Stretching came back under new names. Departures stretched its rail to a buffer, and Sill set its plates on posts. The skeptic said Sill's posts "broke the round-14a lesson ('shrink or add, never stretch') under another name".
- Convergence. The field shares the rail with a NOW lamp, the To do row (amber 'was due', square tick, NOW rule) and the 'Ready · gpt-6-luna · $2.00' foot. The titles were all different this round, and style b found "each line's signature device visible at thumbnail size". Desk, Settled and Quote all now open on a cased glass with a cursor or tube (skeptic a).

**Titles.**
- Heat a: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Trued) was best or joint best in all eight notes. 'Give Vera something to plan.' on Desk's glass with the cursor was its near equal, and the most CRT setting. 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' (Manual) was a close third, with the best measure: one line, the full stop in the light. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Settled) collides with the Send button. 'Tell Vera. / Let's plan.' (Dessau) was style's best and the strongest poster, but a two-sentence slogan as a label to six lenses. 'What should Vera plan?' (Quote) is a retired question form, and failed. 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (Departures) narrows the job to trips, and failed with all eight.
- Heat b: 'What needs a plan? Tell Vera.' (Sill) was best for feedback, soul, system, type and the skeptic. Type praised setting the spoken label on the display line's baseline at a smaller size; the skeptic found the grey 'Tell Vera.' an afterthought. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Waypoint) was best for interaction and usability, and joint best for soul. 'Tell Vera what's on.' (Folio) was style's best and now works as the box's label for usability, interaction and the skeptic, but 'on' is thin, and type failed it. 'Jot it down for Vera to plan.' (Pocket) is warm but long. 'Put it on Vera's list.' (Listing) undersells the job. 'What should Vera plan?' (Plate) is passive, a quiz.

### New features

#### X14b-01 The dialled leader: a round countdown tube with plan days on its bezel, and one straight lit leader from its socket onto NOW (drawing, light effect, light rule)
From **x14b-manual-cross Lit Manual, Dialled** (heat a, 8.05, #2; all 8 top fours, all 8 promise lists).
- What it is:
  - One macro, `dial(entries, size, window=28, socket)`, used by Home (15rem) and Plans (13rem).
  - A graphite case with a printed bezel of 28 day ticks, longer each week.
  - A lamp on each plan day, the next one white-hot, with the day numerals 4, 9, 17 and 24 upright on the glass.
  - The free weekend as a 3px sage arc.
  - The face reads NEXT IN / 2 / DAYS over a hot core.
  - On Home, a 2px phosphor leader with a 4px bloom drops straight from the socket into Coming up's NOW lamp, drawn by the figure, so it lands at any content height.
  - Its rule (19): this is the only lit stroke on the page. Every other NOW line is a 1px trace at 50% that fades by 65% of its run, with only its lamp bright.
  - The caption beside the dial names the next plan and 'then 9, 17 and 24 Oct'.
- Files: x14b-a/variants/x14b-manual-cross/templates/_ui.html (macros `dial_fig` line 388 and `dial` line 405), templates/home.html (the figure and Coming up), templates/plans.html, and sheet.css (rule header lines 16 and 81-85: 'ONE LIT LINE ON HOME'); palettes/x14b-manual-cross.json. Shot: x14b-a/strips/x14b-manual-cross.png (Home, top).
- Praise:
  - Feedback: "the most striking single line in the heat".
  - Soul: "the clearest case of 'light is wired to what it reports' in the heat, and every other NOW is dimmed to a fading trace, so the light is scarce and meaningful".
  - System: "a strict, legible rule for where the light goes".
  - Usability: "the clearest 'what's next' figure in the heat ... above the fold on the phone".
  - Skeptic: "Sill Line's stem done right this time".
- Caveats:
  - The leader is about 245px beside about 150px of dark ground. Every lens would seat the dial at Coming up's head (socket 60-120px above NOW) and fill the bay with the caption, or with 'then 9, 17, 24' as stops on the leader.
  - Set the bezel numerals at 14px or more, in one face (type).
  - Ideas' square radar and Status's small dial should join the same round family (soul).
- Suits: any line with a lit object above a dated list. Desk (its Plans dial, whose case "floats over empty ground", should carry the caption the way this one does, system). Dessau (a lead from its dial onto Coming up's NOW is feedback's fix). Plate's Status dial. Listing, in place of its token dial. The 'one lit line a page' rule suits every line.

### Retired

- **Stretching a rail to meet a fixed end** (Departures, Terminus's 'every rail ends on a buffer', To do's rail run about 230px to the Ready buffer). This is the 14a "shrink or add, never stretch" lesson broken by a system rule. Every lens in heat a marked it, and it held the line level with its parent. A rail ends at its last row; the buffer sits right after it; Ready goes in the page foot.
- **Plates on bare posts** (Sill Line, Wired's fix for 14a's stretched plates). Skeptic: "70px steel stilts ... an unfinished bar chart ... broke the round-14a lesson under another name". Feedback, system and style asked the same. A leader drawn up from the stop to a plate at its content height works (X14b-08). A post is only right when the plate fills it.
- **Starter keys welded flush to the textarea's foot** (Plate, Channelled): it splits the composer and its Tab order, "the one cross that regressed on a basic interaction" (interaction; usability, soul). The order is field, From/Send, then starters.
- **A status line inside the textarea** (Sill, Wired): it "reads as typed or placeholder text" (interaction, usability). It belongs on glass above or below the field (Folio, Settled), or on the box's top lip.
- **L146 the shape legend in the footer**: retired outright after being narrowed in 14a. It survived on Dessau and Waypoint, and soul, style, system, interaction, type and the skeptic all said "the shapes explain themselves". At most, Status keeps a key.
- **L249 the ribbon bookmark for 'you are here'** (Pocket, Bound): read as "an error mark" (interaction) and a stray sub-24px target on every page (usability). A lit dot or a steel underline marks the page.
- **Template-only controls**: Waypoint's ?sort switch that the server ignores and its :target Whose segment. "A control that looks latched and does nothing is the worst state error" (usability; interaction). A filter is a real view parameter or it is not drawn.
- **An unlabelled icon toggle for 'Send where I am'** (Pocket's crosshair, "a mystery icon", skeptic, with a near-invisible focus ring). Keep the words and a visible checkbox state.
- **A status foot whose lamp is dark at rest** (Trued, Yard Lit): every lens. Ready is a steady dim light; breathing means Answering.
- **Light used for a warning**: Dessau's amber-glowing 'LATE 3' tube, and Quote's and Sill's amber setup rings and amber '3'. Light is phosphor and warnings are ink, so late is an amber word or triangle, never glow, and setup is not a warning.
- **The T buffer at the end of every head link** (Trued): narrowed to where a rail truly ends.
- **Titles.** Retire:
  - 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (trips only, failed with all eight lenses).
  - 'Put it on Vera's list.' (a to-do list only).
  - 'What should Vera plan?' (the question form, again on Quote and Plate).
  - 'Send Vera anything to plan.' where a Send button sits under it (Settled; it held on Waypoint).
  - 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' as the box's label (keep it as a poster line only if a one-sentence label sits at the box).
- Shown not to work this round, with no ledger entry of their own:
  - A green wash behind the greeting (Quote's rounded gradient card, Dessau's radial wash, Pocket's broad box wash, Plate's lit slate plate flattening the black).
  - A drawing that labels itself (Plate's 'channel: carries a cut's light to its row', Manual's 'FIG. 1').
  - Restaurant in the late amber (Folio, again).
  - Numbered menu items 1-6 in the bar (Manual).
  - A tiny lit tube placed by rule where the eye does not go (Quote's '4').
  - A head column carried onto inner pages as dead width (Listing).
  - A second glass made to look like Desk's (Settled's status line, by convergence).
  - Inner-page primaries turned into grey outlines (Departures).
  - Moving the primary 'Add' into a dropdown (Quote).
  - Fraunces at hairline weight inside a halo (Folio's title glass).
  - The row afterglow, invisible in stills for a seventh round, except Settled's 2px edge, which no lens remarked. Stop spending fixes on it unless the capture shows a held hover.
